Gregor, Sep 2025: In Aug 2025, Amigo LNG signed a 15-year Sale and Purchase Agreement with Macquarie Group for the offtake of an additional 0.6 mtpa of LNG from the Amigo terminal's first liquefaction train, and announced that it had awarded an EPC contract to Drydocks World for fabrication and delivery of an FLNG (Floating Liquefied Natural Gas) facility and associated FSUs (Floating Storage Units) to the Amigo terminal. With contracts now in place for the full 4.2 mtpa capacity of the first train, Amigo LNG announced in early September 2025 that it expected to make an FID on the project within two months. Commercial operation date for the project's first train has now been pushed back to H2 2028.

GC, Aug 2024: FID still pending, but 20-year contract now signed to supply 3.6 mtpa of LNG to E&H Energy SDN BHD of Malaysia; Gregor, July 2023: Approved for up to 7.8 mtpa by US Dept of Energy. Originally listed as two terminals of 3.9 mtpa each, but as of July 2023 owner's website shows Terminal 1 as 4.2 mtpa and Terminal 2 as 3.6 mtpa. LNG Alliance Pte Ltd Singapore; Epcilon LNG LLC USA

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: Despite hopeful statements from the mayor of Coatzacoalcos in February 2024 speculating on CFE's future investment in the project, there has been no solid news about this export terminal since 2022. All recent media references have referred to CFE's project in the past tense ("CFE had previously announced a potential tender for an LNG facility for Coatzacoalcos"), and have focused instead on the private Coatzacoalcos II LNG export terminal currently being promoted by Comercializadora Aqualita, S.A. and CASARVE Servicios, S.R.L. 
In light of the above, I'm moving the CFE project from proposed to shelved.

GC, Sep 2024: No forward movement on this project since late 2022, although completion of the Southeast Gateway Pipeline in 2025 may give it a new lease on life; move to Shelved in 2025 if no further news?

Gregor, Sep 2025: As of July 2025, construction of Phase 1 was 94% complete, with commercial operations still expected to begin in 2026.

GC, Aug 2024: Full commercial startup of Phase 1 has been delayed until 2026 due to "labor and productivity issues."

Gregor, Sep 2025:  Saguaro Energia's original gas export permit from the US Dept of Energy will expire on Dec 14, 2025. In June 2025, owner Mexico Pacific petitioned USDOE for a seven-year permit extension, through December 2032.

GC, Aug 2024: This project remains stalled in the pre-FID phase, with FID on Train 1 now reportedly delayed till 2025; Gregor,  July 2023: The owner's own name and estimated size for this project has evolved over time. The Mexico Pacific website has changed significantly just within the month of July 2023. At the beginning of the month, the website only mentioned trains 1-3, calling them Phase 1 (trains 1 & 2) and Phase 2 (train 3). By the end of the month, the company had revived talk of trains 4-6, calling them Saguaro Energía II. Compare July 4 version of website -- https://web.archive.org/web/20230704162226/https://mexicopacific.com/saguaro-lng/saguaro-energia/  -- with July 24 version: http://web.archive.org/web/20230724113935/https://mexicopacific.com/saguaro-lng/saguaro-energia/

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: Sempra's latest annual report shows this project to still be under discussion with CFE. Specifically, Sempra states that it has extended the non-binding development agreement with CFE through December 2025 to allow time for negotiation of a more definitive agreement, including a natural gas supply agreement. The 2025 start date shown above is completely obsolete (it comes from an outdated article published in 2020, when the project was originally announced). For the moment, the project remains in the early planning stages and owners haven't provided an alternative start date or clear timeline for the terminal's development.

GC, Sep 2024: Terminal capacity reduced from 3-4 mtpa to 2-3 mtpa in most recent quarterly report (Q2 2024). No other significant developments since Dec 2022. Still listed as an active project on Sempra's website, and DOE's deadline for construction to begin isn't until December 2029 (i.e. much later than other Mexican LNG terminals).
